summary: Eletriptan is an oral triptan for acute treatment of migraine (with or without aura) in adults. As a selective 5-HT1B/1D agonist it constricts cranial vessels and inhibits release of vasoactive neuropeptides in the trigeminal system. It is contraindicated in ischemic or vasospastic cardiovascular, cerebrovascular, and peripheral vascular disease, uncontrolled hypertension, and within 24 hours of ergots or another triptan. Eletriptan is a CYP3A4 substrate: it must not be used within 72 hours of potent CYP3A4 inhibitors, which markedly increase its exposure.
indications: Acute treatment of migraine attacks, with or without aura, in adults

dosage.d: 20 mg or 40 mg as a single dose at onset (40 mg more effective); if headache improves then recurs, a second dose may be taken after at least 2 hours
dosage.t: At onset; repeat once after >=2 h if needed
dosage.n: Max single dose 40 mg; max 80 mg in 24 hours; do not repeat if no response to first dose

admin: Take as soon as possible after onset of migraine headache
Swallow tablet whole; may be taken with or without food
A second dose may be taken after at least 2 hours if the headache returns, but not if there was no response to the first dose
Do not exceed 80 mg in 24 hours
moa: Eletriptan binds with high affinity to 5-HT1B and 5-HT1D receptors (and 5-HT1F). Agonism at vascular 5-HT1B receptors constricts dilated intracranial arteries, while 5-HT1D agonism on trigeminal sensory nerves inhibits release of pro-inflammatory vasoactive neuropeptides (such as CGRP) and reduces nociceptive transmission, relieving the vasodilation and neurogenic inflammation underlying migraine.

History of stroke or transient ischemic attack
Peripheral vascular disease including ischemic bowel disease
Use within 24 hours of an ergotamine/ergot-type drug or another 5-HT1 agonist (triptan)
Use within 72 hours of a potent CYP3A4 inhibitor (ketoconazole, itraconazole, nefazodone, clarithromycin, ritonavir, nelfinavir)

Severe renal or hepatic impairment (not recommended)

monitor: Cardiovascular evaluation in patients with risk factors

preg: There are limited data on use in pregnant women. Eletriptan should be used during pregnancy only if the potential benefit justifies the potential risk to the fetus.
lact: Eletriptan is excreted in human milk. Caution should be exercised; consider avoiding breastfeeding for about 24 hours after a dose to minimize infant exposure.
renal: No dosage adjustment is needed in mild to moderate renal impairment (blood pressure may rise). Eletriptan has not been studied in and is not recommended for patients with severe renal impairment.
hepatic: No dosage adjustment is needed in mild to moderate hepatic impairment. Eletriptan has not been evaluated in severe hepatic impairment and is not recommended in these patients.

major: Potent CYP3A4 inhibitors (ketoconazole, itraconazole, nefazodone, clarithromycin, ritonavir, nelfinavir) - do not use eletriptan within 72 hours
Ergot-containing/ergot-type medications - do not use within 24 hours (additive vasospasm)
Other 5-HT1 agonists/triptans - do not use within 24 hours (additive vasospasm)
interactions.alcohol: No direct pharmacologic interaction; alcohol can independently trigger migraine

monitoring: Cardiovascular evaluation before treatment in patients with risk factors
Frequency of use (medication-overuse headache if used on >=10 days/month)
Serotonergic symptoms when combined with SSRIs/SNRIs
counsel: Take at the first sign of a migraine headache
Do not take more than 80 mg in one day, and do not repeat a dose that did not work
Do not use within 24 hours of another triptan or ergot medicine
Avoid for 3 days after taking strong antifungal or certain antibiotic/antiviral medicines
Stop and seek care for chest pain, pressure, or tightness, or signs of stroke
Frequent use can cause rebound (medication-overuse) headaches
pk: Headache relief often begins within 1-2 hours
Peak plasma concentration about 1.5-2 hours after dosing
Sufficient for a single attack; repeat allowed after >=2 hours

pearls: Higher 5-HT1B/1D affinity and good efficacy; 40 mg is more effective than 20 mg with modestly more side effects
Strong CYP3A4 substrate - the 72-hour rule with potent inhibitors is a key safety point that distinguishes eletriptan from some other triptans
Do not repeat a dose that produced no response to the first dose
Use only after a clear migraine diagnosis; not for prophylaxis, hemiplegic/basilar migraine, or cluster headache
Limit treatment days to reduce medication-overuse headache
missed: Eletriptan is taken only as needed for an acute migraine, so there is no fixed schedule and no missed dose. Take it when a migraine starts, allowing at least 2 hours before any repeat dose and not exceeding 80 mg in 24 hours.
overdose: Overdose may produce hypertension and cardiovascular symptoms. There is no specific antidote; provide supportive care, monitor for at least 20 hours or while symptoms persist (the elimination half-life is about 4 hours but effects can be prolonged), and treat hypertension and vasospastic complications as needed. The effect of dialysis on eletriptan clearance is unknown.
